longDescription:
Gaussmere is an AP Physics C Electricity and Magnetism exam prep app: short lessons, instant questions with worked solutions, spaced review, simulations and timed practice tests for the six calculus-based E&M units.

### Learn By Doing
Six units that follow the course outline: electric charges, fields and Gauss's law; electric potential; conductors and capacitors; electric circuits including RC; magnetic fields and electromagnetism; and electromagnetic induction. 27 short lessons, each with a quick check, and course topic tags on every question.

### Seven Physics Labs
Move charges and watch the field, grow a Gaussian sphere, pull capacitor plates apart, charge an RC circuit, climb an RL ramp, bend a charged particle in a magnetic field, and slide a rod on rails. Every lab ends with a question about what you just did.

### Practice The Exam
270 original questions with full worked solutions, 17 original free-response problems in the four exam question types with part-by-part model answers, and timed 42-question, 85-minute practice tests weighted across the units. Three consecutive practice tests share no questions. Results include a rough practice estimate, never an official score.

### Personal And Private
A short starting check builds your daily plan. Spaced repetition brings back what you are about to forget, and a mistake notebook collects your misses. No account, works offline, worked solutions and references always free.

### Sources
Every lesson lists its references: the College Board course and exam description, OpenStax University Physics and NIST constants.

### Ad-Free Or Earn Credits
Subscribe monthly ($3.99 per month, 7-day free trial for new subscribers) to remove ads. The subscription renews monthly until cancelled. Prefer not to subscribe? Watch short videos to earn credits and unlock features. Cancel any time in your Google Play account settings. If you cancel, you keep ad-free until the end of the period you already paid for, and you will not be charged again.

### Built To Be Honest
All questions and explanations are original and have not been reviewed by a physics teacher. The score estimate is a rough practice estimate. Format details can change; check the College Board exam page.
